court-outer.purpose: The screen ground, applied once at the root behind the grit tile.

court-outer-deep.purpose: Structures resting on the ground: the paddle rack and the scorer toolbar.

court-surface.purpose: Sheets and dialogs, the only surfaces allowed to float.

court-inner.purpose: The playing surface inside the lines, in every court drawing.

court-kitchen.purpose: The non-volley zone, 7ft either side of the net. The mark that makes it a pickleball court.

court-line.purpose: The 2-inch court line, and the only bright fill in the system: primary buttons, selected segments, the on-toggle, court pills, the NEXT UP tab.

court-line-text.purpose: Text and icons on a line-white fill; contrast-tested against #f4f6f2.

ink.purpose: Primary text and icons on the green ground. Same value as the court line.

ink-muted.purpose: Meta lines, row values, captions, disabled reasons. Test-enforced to 4.5:1 on the ground.

danger.purpose: Text-only destructive labels (End, Remove). Never a fill.

ball.purpose: The serving marker and the doubles server number, and nothing else. A test asserts no paddle face uses it.

clock-well.purpose: The dark chip on the net holding the elapsed-match clock.

clock-ink.purpose: Clock digits, and the active-session line on home.

paddle-guard.purpose: The rubber edge guard stroked around every paddle face.

paddle-grip.purpose: The handle wrap under the paddle face.

paddle-grip-text.purpose: Games played, printed on the grip wrap.

pair-tape.purpose: Masking-tape tan, drawn at -6 degrees across two paddles locked as a pair.

face-ochre.purpose: Paddle face 1 of 8. Player identity only. Paired text #2b1d05.

face-coral.purpose: Paddle face 2 of 8. Player identity only. Paired text #2a0c05.

face-paper.purpose: Paddle face 3 of 8. Player identity only. Paired text #1d2a24.

face-sky.purpose: Paddle face 4 of 8. Player identity only. Paired text #0d2638.

face-carbon.purpose: Paddle face 5 of 8. Player identity only. The one dark face; paired text #f1f1ef.

face-lilac.purpose: Paddle face 6 of 8. Player identity only. Paired text #150e26. Darkened from the spec's #b9a6e0 to clear 4.5:1.

face-sand.purpose: Paddle face 7 of 8. Player identity only. Paired text #241c0d. Deepened from the spec's #d9c39a to clear 4.5:1.

face-teal.purpose: Paddle face 8 of 8. Player identity only. Paired text #04201a. Deepened from the spec's #4fb3a5 to clear 4.5:1.

score-call.purpose: The spoken score, serving side first. 92pt on the scorer, 104pt in the win modal, 72pt on the share card. Always tabular.

screen-title.purpose: One per screen, left-aligned at the 16pt text gutter, with a muted 15pt meta line under it.

modal-title.purpose: Dialog titles at 24pt/800 centred; sheet titles at 26pt/700 left-aligned beside a Done button.

section-title.purpose: In-screen section heads such as Rack, with a 13pt muted hint on the same baseline.

row-label.purpose: List rows; player names on court take the same size at 700.

button-label.purpose: All button titles, with an optional 13pt/600 subtitle above at 70% opacity.

body.purpose: Meta lines, descriptions, dialog messages, empty states.

signage.purpose: Painted-signage micro-type: court-number pills and the NEXT UP rack tab. Labels containers only, never sits above a title.

motion.name: court-slot-entry
motion.purpose: Names walking onto a called match: four court slots, staggered 60ms by slot index.

motion.name: rack-enter

motion.name: rack-exit

motion.purpose: Every entry animation downgrades to this when AccessibilityInfo reports Reduce Motion.

motion.name: press-scale

motion.name: screen-push
motion.purpose: The expo-router stack transition; sheets slide up, dialogs fade.

narrative.overview:
The whole app is the thing it is about. The screen ground is outer-court green with the faint grit of sand aggregate rolled into acrylic paint; a match is a real top-down court at real proportions with each name standing in its playing position; the waiting queue is the paddle rack every open-play group already leans against the fence. Nothing is a metaphor for the game — it is a drawing of the game, at a glance, in sun or under court lights. The category default this replaced was white cards, a green button and a plain list of names.

Density is courtside-legible, not dashboard-dense. One screen carries a 34pt title, a small meta line, one court diagram per court, a full-width white action, and the rack. Scores get to be enormous (92–104pt, tabular) because the organiser reads them from arm's length between rallies. Everything else is quiet: text is line-white or a desaturated mint-grey on green, containers are the ground tinted a few percent lighter rather than a new material.

Colour is rationed hard. Green is the world, blue is the court, line-white is the only bright fill, and saturation is reserved almost entirely for the eight paddle faces — one per player, so a person can find themselves on court, in the rack and in the summary without reading. The build carries no shadows at all and no display typeface; depth comes from tonal layering and the type does its work through size and weight alone.
keyCharacteristics: One appearance only: no light/dark switch, same world in either system setting
Real court geometry (44:20, 7ft kitchen) rather than a rounded box
Line-white (#f4f6f2) as the single bright fill, on court lines and primary buttons alike
Eight paddle faces as the only saturated colour, one per player, all test-enforced to 4.5:1
Completely flat: zero shadow declarations in the shipped code
System type only; huge tabular numerals for scores

rules.name: The One Appearance Rule
rules.body: There is no light mode and no dark mode. The court world is identical in either system setting, the status bar is always light, and there is no colour-scheme hook anywhere in the source. Any future surface that branches on appearance is wrong.

rules.name: The Line-White Rule
rules.body: court-line is the only bright fill in the system. If a new surface needs emphasis, it gets line-white or it gets nothing; do not introduce a second accent fill.

rules.name: The Ball Rule
rules.body: ball marks the serve and the server number. It is never a background, a border, a highlight or a paddle face — and a unit test enforces the last of those.

rules.name: The Own Face Rule
rules.body: A player keeps one paddle colour for the whole session, in the rack, on court, and in the summary. Paddle colour is identity, never status; status is carried by outline, ghost and tape instead.

rules.name: The Tint-Not-Material Rule
rules.body: Containers on the ground are line-white at 6–12% alpha with a 8–12% alpha hairline border, not a new colour. Green stays the only ground.

rules.name: The Tabular Score Rule
rules.body: Any digit that changes in place — score, clock, games played, stepper value — is set in tabular numerals so nothing shifts sideways as it counts.

rules.name: The Signage-Labels-Containers Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked micro-type belongs on the tab or pill that names a structure. It never sits above a title as a category line: screen titles are followed by a sentence-case meta line, never preceded by a label.

rules.name: The Real Proportions Rule
rules.body: A court is drawn at 44ft x 20ft with a 7ft kitchen each side of the net. Never fit a court to a convenient box; give it a height or let the aspect ratio decide.

rules.name: The Two-Gutter Rule
rules.body: Text lives at 16pt from the edge, drawings at 12pt. The drawing is always the wider element.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow. If an element needs to feel above its neighbour, deepen it (court-outer-deep), tint it (line-white alpha), or put it behind a scrim.

rules.name: The One Ground Rule
rules.body: The grit texture and the green ground are applied once, at the root. Every screen background and every navigator contentStyle stays transparent.

rules.name: The Sharp Court Rule
rules.body: Court geometry gets 2–4pt corners. Rounding a court into a card destroys the one thing this world is built on.

rules.name: The One Silhouette Rule
rules.body: The paddle shape comes from lib/theme/paddle-shape.ts. The icon generator and the app read the same constants; never redraw it locally.

rules.name: The Inner-View Rule
rules.body: Under NativeWind, a Pressable's style callback is dropped. Visual styling must live on a View inside the Pressable, with press state held in React state. This has broken twice; do not put a background, border or radius on a Pressable directly.

dos: Do style every screen from lib/theme/tokens.ts directly. NativeWind is still installed, but no screen uses its classes and none should.
Do let CourtDiagram keep its 44:20 aspect ratio unless you have a reason to pass an explicit height.
Do give a new player-facing colour a paired text colour that clears 4.5:1, and add it to lib/theme/__tests__/tokens.test.ts so it stays that way.
Do put the one bright line-white fill on the single most important action per screen, and nowhere else.
Do use tabular numerals for every value that changes in place.
Do keep screen and navigator backgrounds transparent so the root grit ground shows through.
Do put press-state visuals on an inner View, per the Inner-View Rule.
Do read Reduce Motion from AccessibilityInfo and crossfade instead of moving.
Do draw paddles from lib/theme/paddle-shape.ts so the app and the generated icons stay identical.
donts: Don't add a light/dark switch, a colour-scheme branch, or a theme toggle. The one appearance is the system.
Don't add a shadow or an elevation value. The build has none; depth is tonal.
Don't introduce a display typeface or a webfont. The system face is the only face.
Don't add a second bright accent fill or a filled destructive button; destructive stays coral text.
Don't spend ball yellow on anything but the serve marker and the server number.
Don't give a paddle face to status. Faces are identity; use outline, ghost and tape for state.
Don't round court geometry past 4pt or fit a court into an arbitrary box.
Don't re-apply the grit texture, or paint an opaque background, inside a screen.
